entries: How many planets are there in the solar system?
There are 8 planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun.
Venus is the hottest planet (about 465 °C) because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat.
Which planet is called the Red Planet?
Mars is called the Red Planet because of iron oxide (rust) on its surface.
Saturn has the most famous rings; Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune also have faint rings.
Which planet is called Earth's twin?
Venus is called Earth's twin because of its similar size.
Which planet has the most moons?
Saturn has the most known moons (well over 140), followed by Jupiter.
The Sun is a star at the centre of our solar system, about 150 million km from Earth. Its light takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach us.
what is the sun made of
How far is the Moon from Earth?
The Moon is on average about 384,400 km from Earth.
Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
Neil Armstrong was the first person on the Moon, on 20 July 1969 (Apollo 11), followed by Buzz Aldrin.
Who was the first person in space?
Yuri Gagarin of the Soviet Union was the first person in space, on 12 April 1961.
Who was the first woman in space?
Valentina Tereshkova of the Soviet Union was the first woman in space, in 1963.
Who was the first Indian woman in space?
Kalpana Chawla was the first Indian-born woman in space (1997). She died in the Columbia disaster in 2003.
A galaxy is a huge system of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity. We live in the Milky Way galaxy.
A black hole is a region where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape.
How long does Earth take to go around the Sun?
Earth takes about 365.25 days to orbit the Sun (one year) and about 24 hours to spin once on its axis (one day).
Seasons happen because Earth's axis is tilted about 23.5°, so different parts get more direct sunlight during the year.
Day and night happen because Earth rotates on its axis once every 24 hours.
why do we have day and night
A solar eclipse happens when the Moon comes between the Sun and Earth, blocking the Sun's light. A lunar eclipse happens when Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon.
What is the highest mountain in the world?
Mount Everest (8,849 m), on the Nepal–China border, is the highest mountain. Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary first climbed it on 29 May 1953.
What is the longest river in the world?
The Nile (about 6,650 km) is usually listed as the longest river; the Amazon is close and carries the most water.
What is the largest desert in the world?
Antarctica is the largest desert overall. The Sahara in Africa is the largest hot desert.
What is the deepest point in the ocean?
The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, Pacific Ocean, is the deepest point, about 10,900 m deep.
What is the largest island in the world?
Greenland is the largest island in the world.
What is the largest lake in the world?
The Caspian Sea is the largest lake by area. Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area, and Lake Baikal the deepest.
The Amazon rainforest in South America is the largest rainforest.
What is the longest wall in the world?
The Great Wall of China is the longest wall, over 21,000 km including all its sections.
What are the Seven Wonders of the World?
The New Seven Wonders (2007): Great Wall of China, Petra (Jordan), Christ the Redeemer (Brazil), Machu Picchu (Peru), Chichen Itza (Mexico), Colosseum (Italy) and Taj Mahal (India).
The equator is the imaginary line around the middle of Earth at 0° latitude, dividing the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
Latitude lines run east–west and measure north–south position (0° at the equator). Longitude lines run north–south and measure east–west position (0° at Greenwich, London).
What are the layers of the Earth?
Earth has the crust (outer), mantle, outer core (liquid) and inner core (solid).
What are the layers of the atmosphere?
From the ground up: troposphere (weather), stratosphere (ozone layer), mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere.
The water cycle: water evaporates, condenses into clouds, falls as precipitation (rain, snow) and collects in rivers, lakes and oceans, then evaporates again.
Global warming is the rise in Earth's average temperature, mainly from greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide released by burning fossil fuels.
The United Nations (UN) was founded on 24 October 1945 to keep world peace. Its headquarters is in New York, and it has 193 member states.
Where is the headquarters of WHO?
The World Health Organization (WHO) is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
The modern Olympic Games began in Athens in 1896 and are held every four years. The five rings stand for five continents.
How many players are there in a cricket team?
A cricket team has 11 players on the field.
How many players are there in a football team?
A football (soccer) team has 11 players on the field, including the goalkeeper.
How many players are there in a hockey team?
A field hockey team has 11 players on the field.
How many players are there in a basketball team?
A basketball team has 5 players on the court.
How many players are there in a volleyball team?
A volleyball team has 6 players on the court.
How many players are there in a kabaddi team?
A kabaddi team has 7 players on the court.
How many squares are on a chessboard?
A chessboard has 64 squares (8 × 8). Each player starts with 16 pieces.
Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing the telephone in 1876.
Thomas Edison made the first practical long-lasting light bulb in 1879 (Joseph Swan worked on it in England at the same time).
The Wright brothers, Orville and Wilbur, made the first powered aeroplane flight on 17 December 1903.
Guglielmo Marconi is credited with inventing radio communication in the 1890s; Jagadish Chandra Bose also did early work on radio waves.
John Logie Baird demonstrated the first working television in 1926.
Charles Babbage designed the first mechanical computer, the Analytical Engine, and is called the father of the computer.
Who invented the World Wide Web?
Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989.
James Watt greatly improved the steam engine in 1769, making it practical; Thomas Newcomen built an earlier one in 1712.
Johannes Gutenberg invented the movable-type printing press around 1440.
Isaac Newton described the law of gravity, published in 1687, reportedly inspired by a falling apple.
Who gave the theory of relativity?
Albert Einstein gave the special theory of relativity (1905) and the general theory (1915).
Electricity wasn't invented by one person; Benjamin Franklin showed lightning is electrical (1752), and Michael Faraday and others made it usable.
Hans Lippershey made the first known telescope in 1608; Galileo improved it and used it to study the sky.
Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896; Marie Curie and Pierre Curie studied it further. Marie Curie won Nobel Prizes in both physics and chemistry.
Sir C. V. Raman discovered the Raman effect (scattering of light) on 28 February 1928 and won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics. 28 February is National Science Day in India.
William Shakespeare wrote Romeo and Juliet. He also wrote Hamlet, Macbeth and Othello.
The Ramayana was written by the sage Valmiki.
The Mahabharata is traditionally credited to the sage Vyasa. It includes the Bhagavad Gita.
Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa, which hangs in the Louvre, Paris.
